title: Global Sell-Off
excerpt: European markets closed lower, while US markets are trading sharply down, which may impact Indian markets tomorrow. The decline in global equities, along with rising volatility, suggests a cautious approach for Indian investors.

What happened

European markets, such as the FTSE 100, closed down 1.02%, while US markets, including the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, are trading down 3.70% and 5.28% respectively. The Dow Jones is also down 1.93%, indicating a broad-based sell-off. The USD/INR is down 0.66% to 92.66, which could support Indian equities, but the rise in India VIX by 11.24% to 17.32 suggests rising volatility and caution among investors.

Our view

cautious Analyst board aligned (3 of 3 views)

  • The house stance is cautious, with a conviction of 3-4 out of 5, due to the sharp decline in global equities and rising volatility. The momentum strategist and risk manager are cautious, citing limited breadth and event risk. How the analyst board voted
  • Momentum strategist: cautious, conviction 3/5. Nifty (+2.27%) and Sensex (+2.30%) rallied strongly while global equity indices fell sharply (S&P -3.70%, Nasdaq -5.28%), indicating domestic momentum but limited breadth (IT flat, VIX up 11%). A weaker USD/INR (-0.66%) and falling US 10Y yields (-2.77%) are supportive for Indian inflows, yet the broader risk-off tone (Europe down, US sell‑off) tempers upside. Commodities are mixed – oil up modestly, gold down sharply, crypto up slightly – and rising volatility (India VIX +11%) suggests keeping risk exposure measured.
  • Risk manager: cautious, conviction 3/5. India’s rally (+2.3%) comes with an 11% jump in India VIX, signalling heightened volatility ahead of the F&O expiry and global equity sell‑off. US markets are sharply down (S&P -3.7%, Nasdaq -5.3%) and upcoming US GDP and tech‑outage headlines add event risk that could spill into emerging markets. A modest INR appreciation (USD/INR -0.66%) and a rise in Brent crude (+0.57%) could pressure import‑heavy stocks, tempering the bullish momentum.
  • Macro economist: cautious, conviction 4/5. The sharp decline in global equities, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq down 3.70% and 5.28% respectively, may weigh on Indian markets The increase in India VIX by 11.24% suggests rising volatility and caution among investors However, the strength in Nifty Bank, up 4.19%, and the decline in USD/INR by 0.66% could provide some support to Indian equities
